methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
REGENT Craft is a Series A-stage transportation company that has raised $60M to date. The valuation universe consists of 8 private frontier-tech peers in transportation (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero), with no direct public comparables available.

Given the early stage and heterogeneity of the peer set, only one valuation method proved applicable: stage-progression analysis. Using the $60M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-round progression yields an implied valuation of $120M. A peer-median approach was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the transportation sector—only three transportation peers exist broadly, and none met the narrow filtering criteria necessary to establish a reliable median.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, with $120M as the central estimate. This range reflects the methodological constraint of relying on a single applicable approach. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable public benchmarks, the limited depth of private peer data at this stage, and inherent variability in stage-progression multiples across capital cycles. Additional data on similar-stage fundraising rounds and revenue traction (if material) would strengthen confidence in this valuation.
